title: A Balanced Committee
statement: A club has $10$ men and $10$ women. In how many ways can it choose a committee (of any size, possibly empty) with equally many men and women?
insight: Swap one side: pick the men who are IN and the women who are OUT. Equal counts means exactly 10 people are picked from 20, so the answer is C(20,10).
redHerring: Computing Σ C(10,k)² term by term.
hints: The answer is $\sum_k \binom{10}{k}^2$. Is there a single binomial coefficient equal to it?
Choosing $k$ women is the same as choosing which $10-k$ women are left out.
Mark the men on the committee and the women off it. How many people are marked?
solution: For a committee with $k$ men and $k$ women, mark the $k$ men on it and the $10-k$ women not on it. That marks exactly $10$ of the $20$ people, and every set of 10 marked people arises from exactly one balanced committee. So the count is $\binom{20}{10} = 184{,}756$ (Vandermonde's identity).
